subject: Game Theory
title: Carbon Markets
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Carbon Markets.

hook.text: Pollution has no price tag. A factory dumps CO2 for free. What if you made companies buy the right to pollute?

buildup.text: Cap-and-trade caps total emissions, then auctions permits. Companies that cut pollution cheaply sell permits to others.

discovery.text: The US acid rain program used this in 1990: SO2 emissions dropped 50% at one-tenth the predicted cost.

twist.text: Europe's carbon market struggled: too many free permits crashed the price to zero. The mechanism needs scarcity to work.

climax.text: After reforms tightened supply, EU carbon prices rose from €5 to over €80. Mechanism design details determine success.

punchline.text: Price the pollution and the market cuts it.

quiz.question: Why did Europe's early carbon market fail?
options: Too many free permits destroyed the price signal
Carbon is too hard to measure
